transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on what's actually wrong. If it turns out to be the drive belt, as seems most likely, that's usually a cheap and simple repair and well worth doing even on a 9-year-old machine. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drive belt [belt-driven machines ONLY]. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
I turned it by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumble. It doesn't feel stiff or rough at all.
Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

I'm not sure that's the right test, as the drum doesn't turn at all in the normal wash either. I don't hear any motor noise when it should be turning, just some clicking. If you want me to run a spin-only cycle I can, but I'd expect the same result.
Run a spin-only (or rinse and spin) programme with the washing in. Does the drum spin up properly on that programme?

As I said, the drum doesn't turn at all on any programme, so I'd expect spin-only to do the same. I can run it if you still want me to. I should also mention that a few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell from the machine, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. No, there's no need to run a spin-only cycle now, as it wouldn't tell us anything more. Given the hot electrical smell you noticed a few weeks ago, it's best not to keep running the machine and to leave it switched off at the wall for now. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
